question: How can we emulate the Prophet's pure heart when his heart was purified miraculously?
asked: We are supposed to have a pure heart, a qalb saleem, and to emulate the Prophet ﷺ. But his heart was cleansed and purified in a supernatural manner, and Allah fortified it with iman. Given that his heart is our role model, how can we possibly follow him when he has reached a level that we can never expect to reach?
answer:
Now, this is a very beautiful question. And it is a question where you can sense, inshaAllah ta'ala, that our brother has a sincere love, and he's worried that he's not going to get to that status or that station, because obviously our Prophet ﷺ is who he is. And where are we in this regard?

And he mentions the issue of qalb saleem, and that's a very deep and profound topic. On the topic of qalb saleem I have actually given a number of khutbahs and talks; you can find them online. But just to summarize: what our brother is referencing is that the Prophet Ibrahim (alayhi al-salam) said in the Qur'an that on the Day of Judgment, on that day, neither wealth nor money will benefit anybody. The Prophet Ibrahim made an exception, and he said: except for the one who came in front of Allah with a pure heart, qalb saleem, with a pure heart. And Allah mentions the Prophet Ibrahim and praises him when Allah says that Ibrahim came to Allah with a qalbun saleem.

Now, of course, the term qalb is a reference to the spiritual heart. It is not a reference to the physical, pulsating heart; this is a physical organ. When the Qur'an mentions qalb, when the Prophet mentions qalb, there is a spiritual inner reality to our existence. We will never understand it. It's not something that is located in a particular place in time, but it is located inside of us.

And the Arabic word qalb actually means, technically, that which is inside. Qalb is that which is inside. Also, by the way, the term also indicates fluttering. It indicates vacillation. It indicates turning round. And so our heart is called qalb because, number one, it is inside of us, literally and spiritually. And number two, because the qalb keeps on changing. One day you have the highest level of courage, the next day you're scared. One day you have himmah and taqah and strength, the next day you just want to give up. One day your iman is so strong, the next day it's not like that. One day you hate somebody, the next day you will love that person. So the qalb is called qalb because it constantly changes.

And that is why our Prophet ﷺ made du'a to Allah, "Allahumma thabbit qulubana": O Allah, make our hearts firm upon Your worship. If our hearts change in love and hate and whatnot in this world, okay, but they should not change when it comes to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. They should be firm in the worship of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And of course, the word saleem is from the same root as Islam, and it means the absence of evil. Some have translated it as peace, but in reality saleem means the heart that has no evil in it. And the qalbun saleem is called qalb saleem because, number one, it does not have the love of any god besides Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And number two, it does not have any factors in it that prevent the person from worshipping Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. So the doubts that might exist in the heart of the munafiq, or following one's desires lustfully, for example: this is not going to be qalb saleem. Because there are people that believe in Allah, but they have impediments in the worship of Allah. Qalb saleem: he believes in Allah, and none but Allah, as a Lord, and then there are no impediments in the worship of Allah.

And then point number three: that there is no animosity and no hatred for anybody else in this world. You have a pure heart. Qalb saleem is that, to the best of your ability, you do not have jealousy towards any fellow believer, you do not have any hatred, you do not have any arrogance towards any other makhluq of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And if you're able to master these three things, then qalbun saleem has been reached.

And our brother is saying that our Prophet ﷺ has reached a level of qalbun saleem that we cannot reach. And this is obvious; nobody can possibly deny this. And that is why he is our Prophet ﷺ. In fact, Allah says in the Qur'an that one of the reasons why he is so perfect and so chosen is that the Qur'an has come to his qalb: the Holy Spirit, or the trustworthy angel, has come down with the Qur'an upon your qalb. So our dear brother in Islam is asking a legitimate question. How can we possibly compare my qalb and your qalb to the qalb that Allah chose for the Qur'an to come down and be preserved in? In pure Arabic, Allah has revealed the Qur'an to the heart of the Messenger. And our brother is saying, how can we compete with that?

And the response, dear brother in Islam: the goal is not competition. The goal is not even to get to that level, because we know with 'ilm al-yaqin that nobody can get to that level. But the goal is that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala revealed that guiding light. He revealed that nur, He revealed that guidance, and He revealed the Messenger to be the perfect role model so that we have something to look up to. We know we're not going to get to that exact same level, and that's not the goal. The goal is that we keep that level, or that maqam, and that height in our eyes. And we keep that bar, which is raised so high, in our sights all the time. And we try our best in every aspect of our life to come as close to the goal as possible, with the realization that we will never actually achieve it.

You see, our Prophet ﷺ is called a qudwatun hasanah. And qudwatun hasanah literally means a good role model, a perfect role model. Allah did not reveal the Qur'an to the Prophet ﷺ so that all of us are going to be exactly like him. Allah revealed it to him so that all of us can attempt to emulate him, so that we can take him as a qudwatun hasanah.

And of course he was aided miraculously, because he is the Prophet of Allah. He is the chosen; he is the Mustafa. And what does Mustafa mean? Inna Allaha istafa Adama wa Nuhan wa ala Ibrahima wa ala 'Imrana 'ala al-'alamin. Allah has chosen specific people. Istafa means to take apart and to purify. So Allah has chosen certain prophets and certain families. The family of Ibrahim has been chosen, and the family of 'Imran has been chosen, and specific people in that lineage Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala has raised in rank and purified.

And therefore our Prophet ﷺ was indeed given a miracle. Of the many miracles he was given is that as a child, his heart was opened up and cleansed miraculously. And of course these reports are in the seerah books of Ibn Hisham, and the Qur'an references it as well: Alam nashrah laka sadrak is referencing here that the Prophet's heart was purified with zamzam water in a canister of gold; it was purified, and any evil that was in it was taken out. And this spiritual operation was actually done twice: firstly when he was a child, and then secondly, on the night of Isra' and Mi'raj, he was fortified once again. And of course, this is something we expect: that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala will honor our Prophet ﷺ and fortify his iman and give him a qalbun saleem.

And even in the hadith of Bukhari as well, our Prophet ﷺ mentioned that every one of us has an evil shaytan that's trying to misguide us, and that shaytan has been with us since we were born. And Aisha said, "O Messenger of Allah, even you?" And he said, "Yes, even me, but Allah has helped me, so that my qarin has converted to Islam, and he only commands good things." This is a divine thing. Of course, we expect our Prophet ﷺ to be blessed in this regard.

So my dear brother in Islam, I sense your love for our Prophet ﷺ. I sense your fear at being distant from him. But I can only assure you with the assurance that our Prophet ﷺ gave to a man that came to him and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I don't have that much sadaqah, and I don't have that much salah and siyam, but I have a love for Allah 'azza wa jall and His Messenger. My heart has love for Allah and His Messenger." And our Prophet ﷺ said, "You shall be with those whom you love." You shall be with those whom you love.

So the goal is not to ever try to achieve that exact level. The goal is to keep on striving. And innama al-a'malu bil-niyyat: Allah will see your effort and your dedication.

This is the beauty of our faith, dear brother in Islam. Listen to this carefully. Every single boss or friend or life partner or colleague or human being will judge you by the final product. Nobody judges by the effort you put in. Your professor doesn't care how many hours you studied; he wants to see the result on the exam. If it so happened that you didn't study at all and you just happened to know the answers, you ace it. And there are others that studied the whole semester, and for whatever reason the question was difficult and they weren't able to answer. You're not rewarded by effort in this world, but in the eyes of Allah, you are rewarded by effort. You're rewarded by dedication, by sincerity.

Therefore, dear brother in Islam, put in the effort, be sincere, do each and every good deed. And in particular, of the deeds that you should do to be with the Prophet ﷺ, I will mention two things that are explicitly mentioned in the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ to be in the company of the Prophet ﷺ.

Number one: our Prophet ﷺ asked one of his servants, "What do you want me to give you?" And the servant was smart. He didn't say any money, any horse. He said, "I want to be with you in Jannah, O Messenger of Allah." And so the Prophet ﷺ said, "Help me to help you in this cause by lots of sajdas." So our dear brother wants to be close to our Prophet ﷺ, and the way to do that is, number one, extra sajdas. Lots of nafl salah: make sure you're praying the regular fard, tahajjud prayers, nafl salah, your sunnah, the ratibah. Make sure that that is done.

And number two, our Prophet ﷺ explicitly said in the hadith, aqrabukum minni manzilan yawm al-qiyamah: the closest of you to me in my manzil (you're not going to get to that manzil, but the closest) are who? Ahasinukum akhlaqan, the best of you in manners. So monitor your manners, control your anger, speak good words, do not get angry at people. Don't be sarcastic and put people down. Give better than what people expect, and expect from others less than what is due unto you. And always be the better of the two in any situation.

These are the two things, and there are more, but of course time is limited. You're asking about trying to achieve as close proximity as possible; that will be done by lots of sajdas and by good akhlaq.

And so to respond to your question, dear brother in Islam: aim and strive and put in the effort, and realize that the goal is not to get to that level with your actions; that will never happen. **The goal is that Allah will see your sincerity, Allah will see your efforts, and Allah will reward you to be in the company of the Prophet ﷺ.** We ask Allah 'azza wa jall that He blesses us to be in the company of the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Judgment and in Jannat al-Firdaws al-A'la.
